DBED5041C4BA Let $Y$ be a closed analytic subset of a complex space $X$, let $\psi $ be smooth strongly $q$-convex on $Y$, and let $\delta >0$ be continuous on $Y$. There are a neighborhood $V$ of $Y$ and a smooth strongly $q$-convex function $\varphi $ on $V$ such that \[  \psi \leq \varphi |_ Y<\psi +\delta .  \] Proof. Take $R$ from lemma 9.49.2 and the stratification of lemma 9.49.3 . Start with any global smooth extension $f_{-1}$ of $\psi $. We construct $f_ k$ smooth on $X$, strongly $q$-convex when restricted to $Y$, and strongly $q$-convex on an open neighborhood $G_ k$ of $Z_ k$. Choose also a closed neighborhood $C_ k$ of $Z_ k$ contained in $G_ k$, increasing with $k$, with $C_{-1}=G_{-1}=\varnothing $. Arrange 8FAB545D8919 9.49.5 \begin{equation}  0\leq (f_ k-f_{k-1})|_ Y<2^{-k-2}\delta , \qquad \operatorname {supp}(f_ k-f_{k-1}) \subset \{ R<2^{-k}\} \setminus C_{k-1}. \end{equation} The closed set $E_ k=Z_ k\setminus G_{k-1}$ lies in the smooth stratum $Z_ k\setminus Z_{k-1}$. Cover it by locally finite relatively compact embedding patches, with supports disjoint from $C_{k-1}$ and inside $\{ R<2^{-k}\} $. In each ambient patch flatten $Z_ k$ to $w_\lambda =0$, with $w_\lambda $ the normal holomorphic coordinates. Choose nonnegative smooth $\theta _\lambda $ of compact support in these patches whose sum is one near $E_ k$. Set 6F7888367208 9.49.6 \begin{equation}  f_ k=f_{k-1}+\sum _\lambda b_\lambda ,\qquad b_\lambda =\theta _\lambda \varepsilon _\lambda ^3 \log (1+\varepsilon _\lambda ^{-4}|w_\lambda |^2). \end{equation} All weights have nonnegative ambient extensions, as above. We give the estimates and the simultaneous choice of constants. On any fixed compact ambient overlap, all coordinate maps, weights and their first two derivatives are bounded. For $0<\varepsilon <1/2$, \[  0\leq \varepsilon ^3\log (1+\varepsilon ^{-4}|w|^2) \leq C\varepsilon ^3(1+|\log \varepsilon |), \qquad |d\log (1+\varepsilon ^{-4}|w|^2)|\leq C\varepsilon ^{-2}.  \] The logarithm is plurisubharmonic. Product differentiation therefore gives the uniform lower Levi bound 3ACE50D93223 9.49.7 \begin{equation}  Hb_\lambda \geq -C\varepsilon _\lambda I. \end{equation} Indeed the cutoff Hessian costs $O(\varepsilon ^3(1+|\log \varepsilon |))$ and its two first-derivative cross terms cost $O(\varepsilon )$; the remaining term is nonnegative. These bounds also hold after holomorphic changes to another embedding: extend the finitely many $w_\lambda $ holomorphically and choose nonnegative local extensions of the weights. Along $Y$ take a strongly $q$-convex extension of $f_{k-1}|_ Y$. Its strict positive eigenvalue margin on a smaller compact piece is positive. Because $Y$ is closed, these pieces may be chosen locally finite in $X$, by adding $X\setminus Y$ to the covering. The error bound ( 9.49.7 ) preserves that margin when the finitely many relevant $\varepsilon _\lambda $ are small. This retains the required positivity along all of $Y$; the function is unchanged on a neighborhood of $C_{k-1}$ by the support condition. We do not require preservation on the whole open $G_{k-1}$, where a strict margin could tend to zero at its boundary. Nor do we assume positivity is stable under arbitrary $q$-convex sums. At a point of $Z_ k$, all the normal functions involved vanish, so the logarithms and their first derivatives vanish. Consequently there is the exact ambient formula there \[  Hf_ k=Hf_{k-1}+\sum _\lambda \theta _\lambda \varepsilon _\lambda ^{-1}(dw_\lambda )^*dw_\lambda .  \] Choose a patch $\mu $ with $\theta _\mu >0$ at a point of $E_ k$. The restriction of $Hf_{k-1}$ to $TZ_ k$ has a positive subspace $F$ of dimension $\max (0,k-q+1)$, by restriction from $Y$. The $\mu $ Gram form is positive definite on the normal directions and zero on $TZ_ k$. If there are no normal directions, the required ambient positivity already follows from this restriction, and no domination is necessary. Otherwise, on $F\oplus N$ write the first block's lower bound as $a>0$, the mixed-block norm as $b$, the normal lower bound as $-c$, and the Gram normal lower bound as $d>0$. Then \[  (Hf_{k-1}+t(dw_\mu )^*dw_\mu )(x+y,x+y) \geq \tfrac a2|x|^2+(td-c-2b^2/a)|y|^2.  \] For $F=0$ only the normal bound $td-c$ is required. Taking $t=\theta _\mu /\varepsilon _\mu $ sufficiently large therefore gives $\max (0,k-q+1)+N_\mu -k\geq N_\mu -q+1$ positive directions. The other Gram forms are nonnegative. Compact smaller pieces where $\theta _\mu $ is bounded below give one sufficient upper bound on $\varepsilon _\mu $, and continuity extends positivity to their neighborhoods. At points of $Z_ k\cap G_{k-1}$ the exact Gram formula adds a semipositive form to an already strongly $q$-convex ambient extension, so positivity there persists without a small-error estimate. All the smallness choices can be made simultaneously. Refine the above compact pieces and the preservation pieces to a locally finite family with compact closures. Each meets only finitely many bump supports, and each compact bump support meets only finitely many pieces. On a preservation piece choose the sum of the error bounds less than half its strict margin. On a new-stratum piece choose the designated $\varepsilon _\mu $ below its normal-domination bound. Each parameter is subject to finitely many positive upper bounds. Local finiteness gives stationarity on a neighborhood of $K$: use the union of $\operatorname {int}C_ j$ and $\{ R>\eta /2\} $, and then take $2^{-k}<\eta /2$. Thus $f=\lim f_ k$ is smooth. Every neighborhood $O$ of $Y$ contains an open strongly $q$-complete neighborhood $V$ of $Y$. The compact portion of $\partial W$ in that sublevel has finite lower bound for $v$, since it is disjoint from $Y$. Thus a finite lower bound on $\chi $ makes $u>1$ there. There is a smooth nondecreasing function $b(t)$ on $[1,\infty )$ dominating $B_{j+2}+1$ on $[j,j+1]$: interpolate the larger values $B_{j+4}+1$ with a fixed smooth increasing step function flat at both ends. For $q=1$ the ambient $V$ carries a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic exhaustion. An open subset of the subspace $A$ has the form $A\cap \Omega _ U$, so this choice of ambient open set is possible. Now $U$ is closed analytic in $\Omega _ U$. Apply theorem 9.49.8 there, and, for the last assertion, proposition 9.49.9 with $Y=U$. Every resulting $V\subset \Omega _ U$ contains $U$, so $A\cap V=U$. This equality concerns this ambient restriction, not a neighborhood of all of the original $A$. $\square$

title: Proposition 9.49.4
section: 9.49 Convex functions near analytic subspaces
text: Proposition 9.49.4 . DBED5041C4BA Let $Y$ be a closed analytic subset of a complex space $X$, let $\psi $ be smooth strongly $q$-convex on $Y$, and let $\delta >0$ be continuous on $Y$. There are a neighborhood $V$ of $Y$ and a smooth strongly $q$-convex function $\varphi $ on $V$ such that \[  \psi \leq \varphi |_ Y<\psi +\delta .  \] Proof. Take $R$ from lemma 9.49.2 and the stratification of lemma 9.49.3 . Start with any global smooth extension $f_{-1}$ of $\psi $. We construct $f_ k$ smooth on $X$, strongly $q$-convex when restricted to $Y$, and strongly $q$-convex on an open neighborhood $G_ k$ of $Z_ k$. Choose also a closed neighborhood $C_ k$ of $Z_ k$ contained in $G_ k$, increasing with $k$, with $C_{-1}=G_{-1}=\varnothing $. Arrange 8FAB545D8919 9.49.5 \begin{equation}  0\leq (f_ k-f_{k-1})|_ Y<2^{-k-2}\delta , \qquad \operatorname {supp}(f_ k-f_{k-1}) \subset \{ R<2^{-k}\} \setminus C_{k-1}. \end{equation} The closed set $E_ k=Z_ k\setminus G_{k-1}$ lies in the smooth stratum $Z_ k\setminus Z_{k-1}$. Cover it by locally finite relatively compact embedding patches, with supports disjoint from $C_{k-1}$ and inside $\{ R<2^{-k}\} $. In each ambient patch flatten $Z_ k$ to $w_\lambda =0$, with $w_\lambda $ the normal holomorphic coordinates. Choose nonnegative smooth $\theta _\lambda $ of compact support in these patches whose sum is one near $E_ k$. Set 6F7888367208 9.49.6 \begin{equation}  f_ k=f_{k-1}+\sum _\lambda b_\lambda ,\qquad b_\lambda =\theta _\lambda \varepsilon _\lambda ^3 \log (1+\varepsilon _\lambda ^{-4}|w_\lambda |^2). \end{equation} All weights have nonnegative ambient extensions, as above. We give the estimates and the simultaneous choice of constants. On any fixed compact ambient overlap, all coordinate maps, weights and their first two derivatives are bounded. For $0<\varepsilon <1/2$, \[  0\leq \varepsilon ^3\log (1+\varepsilon ^{-4}|w|^2) \leq C\varepsilon ^3(1+|\log \varepsilon |), \qquad |d\log (1+\varepsilon ^{-4}|w|^2)|\leq C\varepsilon ^{-2}.  \] The logarithm is plurisubharmonic. Product differentiation therefore gives the uniform lower Levi bound 3ACE50D93223 9.49.7 \begin{equation}  Hb_\lambda \geq -C\varepsilon _\lambda I. \end{equation} Indeed the cutoff Hessian costs $O(\varepsilon ^3(1+|\log \varepsilon |))$ and its two first-derivative cross terms cost $O(\varepsilon )$; the remaining term is nonnegative. These bounds also hold after holomorphic changes to another embedding: extend the finitely many $w_\lambda $ holomorphically and choose nonnegative local extensions of the weights. Along $Y$ take a strongly $q$-convex extension of $f_{k-1}|_ Y$. Its strict positive eigenvalue margin on a smaller compact piece is positive. Because $Y$ is closed, these pieces may be chosen locally finite in $X$, by adding $X\setminus Y$ to the covering. The error bound ( 9.49.7 ) preserves that margin when the finitely many relevant $\varepsilon _\lambda $ are small. This retains the required positivity along all of $Y$; the function is unchanged on a neighborhood of $C_{k-1}$ by the support condition. We do not require preservation on the whole open $G_{k-1}$, where a strict margin could tend to zero at its boundary. Nor do we assume positivity is stable under arbitrary $q$-convex sums. At a point of $Z_ k$, all the normal functions involved vanish, so the logarithms and their first derivatives vanish. Consequently there is the exact ambient formula there \[  Hf_ k=Hf_{k-1}+\sum _\lambda \theta _\lambda \varepsilon _\lambda ^{-1}(dw_\lambda )^*dw_\lambda .  \] Choose a patch $\mu $ with $\theta _\mu >0$ at a point of $E_ k$. The restriction of $Hf_{k-1}$ to $TZ_ k$ has a positive subspace $F$ of dimension $\max (0,k-q+1)$, by restriction from $Y$. The $\mu $ Gram form is positive definite on the normal directions and zero on $TZ_ k$. If there are no normal directions, the required ambient positivity already follows from this restriction, and no domination is necessary. Otherwise, on $F\oplus N$ write the first block's lower bound as $a>0$, the mixed-block norm as $b$, the normal lower bound as $-c$, and the Gram normal lower bound as $d>0$. Then \[  (Hf_{k-1}+t(dw_\mu )^*dw_\mu )(x+y,x+y) \geq \tfrac a2|x|^2+(td-c-2b^2/a)|y|^2.  \] For $F=0$ only the normal bound $td-c$ is required. Taking $t=\theta _\mu /\varepsilon _\mu $ sufficiently large therefore gives $\max (0,k-q+1)+N_\mu -k\geq N_\mu -q+1$ positive directions. The other Gram forms are nonnegative. Compact smaller pieces where $\theta _\mu $ is bounded below give one sufficient upper bound on $\varepsilon _\mu $, and continuity extends positivity to their neighborhoods. At points of $Z_ k\cap G_{k-1}$ the exact Gram formula adds a semipositive form to an already strongly $q$-convex ambient extension, so positivity there persists without a small-error estimate. All the smallness choices can be made simultaneously. Refine the above compact pieces and the preservation pieces to a locally finite family with compact closures. Each meets only finitely many bump supports, and each compact bump support meets only finitely many pieces. On a preservation piece choose the sum of the error bounds less than half its strict margin. On a new-stratum piece choose the designated $\varepsilon _\mu $ below its normal-domination bound. Each parameter is subject to finitely many positive upper bounds. For the value budget, enumerate the supports and additionally require on $Y\cap \operatorname {supp}\theta _\lambda $ \[  b_\lambda <2^{-\lambda -1}2^{-k-2}\delta .  \] The positive minimum of $\delta $ on this compact set and the uniform amplitude bound make this another positive upper bound; an empty intersection imposes none. Their sum proves ( 9.49.5 ). Thus $f_ k$ is strongly $q$-convex on an open set containing $C_{k-1}\cup Z_ k$. Shrink inside this set to a closed neighborhood $C_ k$ of $C_{k-1}\cup Z_ k$, and choose an open $G_ k$ containing $C_ k$ on which the positivity holds. Such shrinkings follow, for example, from the locally finite partition construction in lemma 9.49.1 applied to a closed set and its open neighborhood. The sequence is stationary near every compact subset of $X$. For a compact $K$, local stationarity of the stratification puts $K\cap Y$ in the interior of some $C_ j$. The remaining compact set $K\setminus \operatorname {int}C_ j$ is disjoint from $Y$, so $R$ has a positive minimum $\eta $ there; if this set is empty use any $\eta >0$. For large $k$ the support condition in ( 9.49.5 ) excludes this compact set, and it excludes $C_ j$ as well. Local finiteness gives stationarity on a neighborhood of $K$: use the union of $\operatorname {int}C_ j$ and $\{ R>\eta /2\} $, and then take $2^{-k}<\eta /2$. Thus $f=\lim f_ k$ is smooth. Near every point of $Y$ it is eventually equal to a strongly $q$-convex $f_ k$, and hence is strongly $q$-convex on some neighborhood $V$ of $Y$. Summing the positive value budgets gives $\psi \leq f|_ Y<\psi +\delta $ (in fact the total increment is at most $\delta /2$). Restrict $f$ to $V$. $\square$

title: Theorem 9.49.8
section: 9.49 Convex functions near analytic subspaces
text: Theorem 9.49.8 . 9EBE244C8709 Let $Y$ be a closed strongly $q$-complete analytic subset of a complex space $X$. Every neighborhood $O$ of $Y$ contains an open strongly $q$-complete neighborhood $V$ of $Y$. More precisely, if $\psi $ is a smooth strongly $q$-convex exhaustion on $Y$ and $\delta >0$ is continuous, the neighborhood can carry a smooth strongly $q$-convex exhaustion $\widetilde\psi $ with \[  \psi \leq \widetilde\psi |_ Y<\psi +\delta .  \] Proof. The empty case is immediate. Extend $\psi $ approximately by proposition 9.49.4 , obtaining $\varphi $ strongly $q$-convex on $W_0$ and the displayed inequalities on $Y$. Adding the same constant to $\psi ,\varphi $ first, assume $\varphi |_ Y>2$. We first arrange properness on a closed neighborhood. Let $r\geq 0$ be a smooth exhaustion of $X$. For every integer $j$, $r$ is bounded on the compact set $Y\cap \{ \varphi \leq j\} $. Choose an increasing continuous $a$ such that $r<a(\varphi )$ on $Y$. There is an open neighborhood $W_1$ of $Y$ with \[  \overline W_1\subset W_0\cap \{ \varphi >1,\  r<a(\varphi )\} .  \] The local partition/shrinking construction above supplies this closed neighborhood inclusion. On $\overline W_1$, each closed $\varphi $-sublevel is compact: it is closed in $X$, lies in $W_0$, and has $r\leq a(t)$ when $\varphi \leq t$. Choose a neighborhood $W$ with $\overline W\subset W_1\cap O$. Its boundary is disjoint from $Y$. Use $v$ from lemma 9.49.2 . We choose a smooth convex increasing $\chi $ so that, on $W\setminus Y$, \[  u=v+\chi (\varphi )  \] has a common positive subspace with $H\varphi $ in every required ambient patch, and $u>1$ on $\partial W$. Here are all bounds needed for this choice. The compact sets $\overline W\cap \{ \varphi \leq j\} $ have finite ambient covers on which $H\varphi $ is positive on a fixed subspace $F$ of codimension at most $q-1$, with lower bound $\lambda >0$, whereas $Hv\geq -CI$. After shrinking, the same $F$ works throughout each patch. Patches on which $v$ is identically $-\infty $ need no bound, since the final correction below is identically zero there. Thus $\chi '\geq (C+\lambda )/\lambda $ gives $Hu|_ F\geq \lambda I$, because the $\chi ''$ term is nonnegative. The compact portion of $\partial W$ in that sublevel has finite lower bound for $v$, since it is disjoint from $Y$. Thus a finite lower bound on $\chi $ makes $u>1$ there. Increase all these bounds to a positive nondecreasing sequence $B_ j$. There is a smooth nondecreasing function $b(t)$ on $[1,\infty )$ dominating $B_{j+2}+1$ on $[j,j+1]$: interpolate the larger values $B_{j+4}+1$ with a fixed smooth increasing step function flat at both ends. Set $\chi (t)=B_3+2+\int _1^ t b(s)\, ds$ on this interval and extend convexly and increasingly to $\mathbb R$. Then $\chi '$ has all the required derivative bounds, and the last unit integration interval (or the initial constant for $1\leq t\leq 2$) gives all value bounds. The extension to the left can use a constant positive derivative near1; the chosen interpolation may be constant there. Choose a smooth convex nondecreasing $\zeta $ which vanishes for $s\leq 1/3$ and has derivative one for $s\geq 1$. For example integrate a smooth increasing function from zero to one on $[1/3,1]$. The function $\theta (t)=\zeta (-1/t)$, $t<0$, is nonnegative, convex and nondecreasing, vanishes for $t\leq -3$, and tends to $+\infty $ as $t\uparrow 0$. Put \[  V=\{ x\in W:u(x)<0\} ,\qquad \widetilde\psi =\varphi +\theta (u).  \] At $Y$ use $u=-\infty $ and $\theta (u)=0$. Since $v\to -\infty $ locally at $Y$, this last term vanishes on a neighborhood of each point of $Y$. Thus $V$ is a neighborhood of $Y$ and $\widetilde\psi $ is smooth everywhere on it, with $\widetilde\psi |_ Y=\varphi |_ Y$. Off $Y$, the chain rule on the common subspace $F$ gives \[  H\widetilde\psi |_ F =H\varphi |_ F+\theta '(u)Hu|_ F +\theta ''(u)|\partial u|_ F^2>0.  \] Thus it is strongly $q$-convex; no arbitrary sum rule is invoked. Finally it is an exhaustion. A sequence in a closed sublevel $\widetilde\psi \leq M$ has $\varphi \leq M$ and hence a subsequence converging in the compact set $\overline W\cap \{ \varphi \leq M\} $. Its limit cannot lie on $\partial W$, where $u>1$. A limit in $Y$ lies inside $V$. Any other limit is in $W\setminus Y$; if $u$ tended to zero, $\theta (u)$ would tend to infinity, a contradiction. The limit therefore belongs to $V$ and its closed sublevel. This proves compactness. Subtract the initial constant if one was added. $\square$

title: Proposition 9.49.9
section: 9.49 Convex functions near analytic subspaces
text: Proposition 9.49.9 . 64118C3BCA67 Let $Y\subset X$ be closed analytic and $U\subset Y$ open. Suppose that for a given compact $L\subset U$ there are a smooth strongly $q$-convex exhaustion $\psi $ on $Y$ and a real $c$ with \[  L\subset \{ \psi <c\} \Subset U.  \] There are a strongly $q$-complete open neighborhood $V$ of $Y$ in $X$, a smooth strongly $q$-convex exhaustion $\widetilde\psi $ on $V$, and a sublevel $V_ b=\{ \widetilde\psi <b\} $ such that \[  L\subset Y\cap V_ b\Subset U.  \] The neighborhood may be required to lie in any prescribed neighborhood of $Y$. This applies, in particular, to each compact $L$ when $U$ is $q$-Runge complete in $Y$. Proof. For nonempty $L$ choose $d>0$ with $\max _ L\psi <c-d$. For empty $L$ any $d>0$ suffices. Apply theorem 9.49.8 with constant error $d/2$. Then $\psi \leq \widetilde\psi |_ Y<\psi +d/2$, so with $b=c$ one has \[  L\subset Y\cap V_ c\subset \{ \psi <c\} \Subset U.  \] Its closure in $Y$ is compact and contained in $U$, which is the asserted relative compactness. In particular $V$ contains all of $Y$; there is no assertion $Y\cap V=U$ for a proper open $U$. $\square$

title: Corollary 9.49.10
section: 9.49 Convex functions near analytic subspaces
text: Corollary 9.49.10 . 4D18CC58062C Let $A$ be closed analytic in an open set $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ N$, and $U\subset A$ a strongly $q$-complete open subset. Choose an open $\Omega _ U\subset \Omega $ with $A\cap \Omega _ U=U$. Every neighborhood of $U$ in $\Omega _ U$ contains a strongly $q$-complete open set $V$ with $A\cap V=U$. For $q=1$ the ambient $V$ carries a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic exhaustion. If $U'\subset U$ is $q$-Runge complete, the exhaustion can additionally have $L\subset A\cap V_ b\Subset U'$ for any specified compact $L\subset U'$. Proof. An open subset of the subspace $A$ has the form $A\cap \Omega _ U$, so this choice of ambient open set is possible. Now $U$ is closed analytic in $\Omega _ U$. Apply theorem 9.49.8 there, and, for the last assertion, proposition 9.49.9 with $Y=U$. Every resulting $V\subset \Omega _ U$ contains $U$, so $A\cap V=U$. This equality concerns this ambient restriction, not a neighborhood of all of the original $A$. $\square$

Manifolds are Hausdorff, second countable and without boundary. Curvature is unscaled, $\mathcal H(f)=\mathrm i\partial  ar\partial f$ and $\mathrm i\Theta (L)=2\pi c_1(L)$. Adjoints and volume are those of the indicated smooth Hermitian metrics. An exhaustion has compact closed sublevels; a finite continuous exhaustion is bounded below (restrict to any one nonempty compact sublevel), so may be shifted to be nonnegative. Strong $q$-convexity means at least $n-q+1$ positive Levi eigenvalues, for an integer $q\geq 1$. Lemma 9.50.1 . 8646B8C271A2 Let $\psi $ be smooth strongly $q$-convex on an $n$-dimensional complex manifold, with $1\leq q\leq n$. For every $\varepsilon >0$ there is a smooth Hermitian metric $\omega $ such that the increasingly ordered eigenvalues of $\mathcal H(\psi )$ satisfy \[  \gamma _1\geq -\varepsilon ,\qquad \gamma _ q=\cdots =\gamma _ n=1.  \] If $\psi $ is an exhaustion, a further smooth conformal change gives a complete Hermitian metric $\widehat\omega =f\omega $, with $f=1+|d\psi |_\omega ^2\geq 1$. Relative to it the sum of any $k$ Levi eigenvalues is at least 6CB1E8CBE35D 9.50.2  egin{equation}  f^{-1} igl (k-q+1-(q-1)\varepsilon  igr ) \qquad (q\leq k\leq n). \end{equation} Here the differential norm uses the associated real Riemannian metric. Proof. Choose any smooth Hermitian metric $\omega _0$ and let $A_0$ be its self-adjoint endomorphism defining $\mathcal H(\psi )$. The ordered eigenvalues $\gamma _ j^0$ are continuous by lemma 10.49.2 , and $\gamma _ q^0>0$. Choose a locally finite partition with supports where $\gamma _ q^0$ has a positive lower bound $a_ j$. The smooth positive function $\eta =\sum _ j	heta _ ja_ j/2$ satisfies $0<\eta \leq \gamma _ q^0$. No global positive minimum is required. Take a smooth nonincreasing cutoff $0\leq  eta \leq 1$ equal to one for $t\leq 1/3$ and zero for $t\geq 2/3$, and put \[  a(t)=(1+\varepsilon ^{-1})\sqrt{1+t^2},\qquad F(t)= eta (t)a(t)+(1- eta (t))t.  \] It is smooth positive, satisfies $F(t)\geq |t|/\varepsilon $ for $t\leq 0$ and $F(t)\geq t$ for $t\geq 0$, and equals $t$ for $t\geq 1$. The exact smooth functional calculus of lemma 10.49.2 makes $A=\eta F[A_0/\eta ]$ a smooth positive endomorphism. Give the base the metric $\omega $ obtained by inserting $A$ into $\omega _0$. At a point its new Levi eigenvalues are \[   rac{\gamma _ j^0}{\eta F(\gamma _ j^0/\eta )}.  \] Each lies in $[-\varepsilon ,1]$ and each labelled $j\geq q$ equals one. Hence the increasingly ordered last $n-q+1$ eigenvalues are one, irrespective of any ordering of the other fractions. When $\psi $ is exhaustive, the conformal metric in the statement satisfies $|d\psi |_{\widehat\omega }^2\leq 1$. It is complete: a Cauchy sequence has bounded $\psi $ by this Lipschitz estimate, lies in a compact sublevel, and has a convergent subsequence; smooth positive local metric comparison identifies its topology with the manifold topology, so Cauchyness gives convergence. This works on each component. Conformal change multiplies every eigenvalue by $f^{-1}$, and any $k$ indices include at least $k-q+1$ of the ones, proving ( 9.50.2 ). $\square$ Lemma 9.50.3 . E85E2E5CB1FF Let $(M,\omega )$ be complete Hermitian and $(G,h)$ a smooth Hermitian holomorphic bundle. In a fixed bidegree $(p,k)$ with $0\leq p\leq n$ and $1\leq k\leq n$, suppose \[  A=[\mathrm i\Theta (G,h),\Lambda _\omega ]+T_\omega \geq I,  \] where $T_\omega $ is the exterior-factor zero-order remainder in theorem 11.48.15 . Every distributionally closed $g\in L^2_{p,k}(M,G)$ has a solution $D''u=g$ with $\| u\| ^2\leq \| g\| ^2$. Its unique minimum-norm solution satisfies $\delta ''u=0$ and is smooth when $g$ is smooth. Moreover a smooth form satisfying $D''u=\delta ''u=0$ on a fixed open set obeys, for compact $K\Subset W$ in that set, 09CCAA35AAF1 9.50.4  egin{equation}  \| u\| _{C^ r(K)}\leq C_{r,K,W}\| u\| _{L^2(W)} \qquad (r\geq 0), \end{equation} using finitely many fixed local frames. No Kähler assumption is needed. Proof. The exact complete-Hermitian domain lemma 6.26.4 supplies the closed maximal $D''$ operators, their maximal formal-adjoint domains and joint compactly supported smooth graph density in every degree/rank. Its assumptions apply to this smooth $h$, including when it contains an arbitrary smooth scalar weight: the cutoff errors are wedge and contraction by $ ar\partial \chi _ R$, whose norms depend only on the complete base metric, not derivatives of that weight. The local smooth-matrix commutator uses only bounds on each compact chart. Thus no global bound on weight derivatives is an extra premise. For compactly supported smooth $v$, the complete Hermitian energy identity theorem 11.48.15 gives \[  \| v\| ^2\leq \int \langle Av,vangle \leq \| D''v\| ^2+\| \delta ''v\| ^2.  \] Pass the first and last terms to the joint graph limit. With $T=D''$ from $(p,k-1)$ and $S=D''$ from $(p,k)$, this proves \[  |\langle g,vangle |^2\leq \| g\| ^2 (\| T^*v\| ^2+\| Sv\| ^2)  \] on the full joint domains. For $k=n$, $S=0$ into the zero space. The equality $(D'')^2=0$ gives $ST=0$ on the maximal domains. The checked closed Hilbert-complex theorem Hilbert-complex solvability from the dual energy estimate gives the solution and bound. The affine solution space has the closed direction $\ker T$, so has a unique minimum orthogonal to that kernel. The preceding $D''$ range lies in this kernel; testing its adjoint shows $\delta ''u=0$. In antiholomorphic degree zero this is automatic. We verify regularity and the quantitative local assertion. At a real covector $\xi $, the principal symbols of $D''$ and $\delta ''$ are exterior multiplication by $\xi ^{0,1}$ and its contraction. Their anticommutator is $|\xi |_\omega ^2I/2$, so the principal symbol of $\Delta ''$ is real scalar and positive, for any smooth Hermitian base and bundle metric. In coordinates its divergence principal form is $	frac 12\int g^{ij}H_{AB}\partial _ jv_ A \overline{\partial _ iv_ B}\, dV$. Integration by parts and absorption of the lower-order terms give, on compactly supported smooth vectors, \[  \| v\| _{H^1}^2\leq C(\| D''v\| ^2+\| \delta ''v\| ^2+\| v\| ^2).  \] Localize a weak solution by a chart cutoff. Smooth-matrix commutator approximation and this bound give a bounded $H^1$ approximation; weak derivative convergence puts it in $H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$. The equation $\Delta ''u=\delta ''g$ has smooth right-hand side. The complete finite-vector divergence regularity theorem interior regularity for elliptic systems in divergence form , followed by Sobolev spaces, duality and local embedding , yields smoothness. For the last assertion, on a slightly larger compact neighborhood the cutoff product rules and $D''u=\delta ''u=0$ bound the initial $H^1$ norm by $C\| u\| _{L^2(W)}$. The quantitative interior estimates for that same divergence system then bound every higher Sobolev norm on successively smaller neighborhoods by the same $L^2$ norm; its right-hand side is zero. The proved local Sobolev embedding gives ( 9.50.4 ). All metrics and coefficients in this last bound are fixed. $\square$ Theorem 9.50.5 . 8AB8E8F1EBBE Let $M$ be strongly $q$-complete and $E$ a holomorphic vector bundle, where $q\geq 1$. Then \[  H^ k(M,\mathcal O(E))=0\qquad (k\geq q).  \] Explicitly, every smooth closed $E$-valued $(0,k)$-form in this range has a smooth primitive. The statement allows non-Kähler manifolds and does not impose curvature positivity on $E$. Proof. The empty manifold, zero bundle, dimension zero and $q>n$ give no nonzero Dolbeault terms in the specified range. Otherwise take a smooth strongly $q$-convex exhaustion $\psi \geq 0$ and use lemma 9.50.1 with $\varepsilon =1/q$. Fix the resulting complete metric $\widehat\omega =f\omega $ once and for all. The pointwise line-curvature coefficient formula in proposition 10.33.6 and ( 9.50.2 ) give, on $(n,k)$ for $k\geq q$, 894DFD0DF9E2 9.50.6  egin{equation}  [\mathcal H(\psi ),\Lambda _{\widehat\omega }] \geq (qf)^{-1}I. \end{equation} Give $E$ a fixed smooth metric, $K_ M$ its induced metric, and put $G=E\otimes K_ M^{-1}$. The fixed smooth Hermitian operators \[  A_0^{(k)}=[\mathrm i\Theta (G),\Lambda _{\widehat\omega }] +T_{\widehat\omega }\otimes I_ G \quad (q\leq k\leq n)  \] have a continuous common norm bound $C(x)\geq 0$, the maximum of their finitely many pointwise norms. This bound is finite on every compact sublevel. All derivatives of the complete conformal metric that occur in $T_{\widehat\omega }$ are already fixed; no uniform bound at infinity or limiting conformal parameter is assumed. Multiplying the bundle norm by a scalar weight cancels in every endomorphism operator norm, so this same $C(x)$ is independent of it. For a convex increasing smooth $\chi $ multiply the metric of $G$ by $e^{-\chi (\psi )}$. Tensor curvature and the chain rule give \[  \mathrm i\Theta (G_\chi )=\mathrm i\Theta (G) +\chi '(\psi )\mathcal H(\psi )I_ G +\chi ''(\psi )\mathrm i\partial \psi \wedge  ar\partial \psi I_ G.  \] The last term is a semipositive scalar curvature, whose operator on $(n,k)$ is nonnegative. Thus its torsion-curvature operator satisfies 1D0C411FD4AC 9.50.7  egin{equation}  A_\chi ^{(k)}\geq  igl (\chi '(\psi )/(qf)-C(x) igr )I. \end{equation} The torsion term has not changed: it acts on the exterior factor and depends only on the fixed base metric, by theorem 11.48.15 . We give a single weight which makes this at least $I$ in all these degrees and makes any specified smooth datum $g$ square integrable. For that datum, after the canonical-form identification below, put \[  a_ j=\int _{\{ j\leq \psi \leq j+1\} }|g|^2\, dV_{\widehat\omega }<\infty .  \] Choose nondecreasing $M_ j\geq 1$ larger than $q\sup _{\{ \psi \leq j+2\} } f(C+1)$ and than $\log (2^{j+2}(1+a_{j+1}))$. A supremum over the empty set imposes no condition. Let $\zeta $ be smooth nondecreasing, zero up to0 and one from1, and set on the real line \[  b(t)=M_0+\sum _{j\geq 0}(M_{j+1}-M_ j)\zeta (t-j),\qquad \chi (t)=\int _0^ t b(s)\, ds.  \] These sums are locally finite. On $[j,j+1]$ one has $\chi '\geq M_ j$, so ( 9.50.7 ) is at least $I$. For $j\geq 1$, $\chi (j)\geq M_{j-1}\geq \log (2^{j+1}(1+a_ j))$, giving \[  \int _ M |g|^2e^{-\chi (\psi )}\, dV_{\widehat\omega } \leq a_0+\sum _{j\geq 1}2^{-j-1}<\infty .  \] The integer bands may overlap on level sets, which only enlarges this upper bound. The construction works for compactly supported data with a weight chosen only from the geometry as well. The canonical identification from $E$-valued $(0,j)$-forms to $G$-valued $(n,j)$-forms is \[  I_ j(a\otimes v)=(a\wedge 	au )\otimes (v\otimes 	au ^{-1}),  \] where $	au $ is a local nonzero holomorphic top form. Transition factors cancel, and appending it on the right makes $I$ commute with $D''$ without a degree sign. The induced canonical/dual metrics make it isometric. Apply lemma 9.50.3 to $I_ kg$ and the chosen weight; pull its smooth primitive back by $I_{k-1}$. This proves smooth analytic vanishing. The exact E-valued Dolbeault resolution comparison corollary 10.43.11 gives the sheaf statement. $\square$ Theorem 9.50.8 . 7B8A55FF470A Let $U$ be a $q$-Runge complete open subset of a strongly $q$-complete manifold $M$: for every compact $L\subset U$ some smooth strongly $q$-convex exhaustion $\psi $ of $M$ has $L\subset \{ \psi <b\} \Subset U$. For every holomorphic vector bundle $E$ and smooth closed $E$-valued $(0,q-1)$-form $h$ on $U$, there is a sequence of global smooth closed forms on $M$ converging to $h$ with all derivatives on every compact subset of $U$. Proof. If $q>n+1$ the form space is zero. If $q=n+1$, all $(0,n)$-forms are closed; multiply $h$ by compact cutoffs on an exhaustion of $U$ and extend by zero to obtain the assertion. Dimension zero and empty $U$ are included. Thus assume $1\leq q\leq n$ and fix a nonempty compact $L\subset U$. Choose $\psi $ as in the hypothesis, shifted to be nonnegative. Compactness gives $b_0<b$ with $L\subset \{ \psi <b_0\} $. Choose a compactly supported smooth $\eta $ in $U$ equal to one on a neighborhood of $\overline{\{ \psi <b\} }$. Under the canonical complex map above, regard $h$ as a $G$-valued $(n,q-1)$-form and set $g=D''(\eta h)$. This extends by zero to a smooth closed global form; its support is compact and contained in $\{ \psi \geq b\} $. u =\chi _0+

title: Lemma 9.50.1
section: 9.50 Bundle cohomology on strongly convex exhaustions
text: Lemma 9.50.1 . 8646B8C271A2 Let $\psi $ be smooth strongly $q$-convex on an $n$-dimensional complex manifold, with $1\leq q\leq n$. For every $\varepsilon >0$ there is a smooth Hermitian metric $\omega $ such that the increasingly ordered eigenvalues of $\mathcal H(\psi )$ satisfy \[  \gamma _1\geq -\varepsilon ,\qquad \gamma _ q=\cdots =\gamma _ n=1.  \] If $\psi $ is an exhaustion, a further smooth conformal change gives a complete Hermitian metric $\widehat\omega =f\omega $, with $f=1+|d\psi |_\omega ^2\geq 1$. Relative to it the sum of any $k$ Levi eigenvalues is at least 6CB1E8CBE35D 9.50.2 \begin{equation}  f^{-1}\bigl (k-q+1-(q-1)\varepsilon \bigr ) \qquad (q\leq k\leq n). \end{equation} Here the differential norm uses the associated real Riemannian metric. Proof. Choose any smooth Hermitian metric $\omega _0$ and let $A_0$ be its self-adjoint endomorphism defining $\mathcal H(\psi )$. The ordered eigenvalues $\gamma _ j^0$ are continuous by lemma 10.49.2 , and $\gamma _ q^0>0$. Choose a locally finite partition with supports where $\gamma _ q^0$ has a positive lower bound $a_ j$. The smooth positive function $\eta =\sum _ j\theta _ ja_ j/2$ satisfies $0<\eta \leq \gamma _ q^0$. No global positive minimum is required. Take a smooth nonincreasing cutoff $0\leq \beta \leq 1$ equal to one for $t\leq 1/3$ and zero for $t\geq 2/3$, and put \[  a(t)=(1+\varepsilon ^{-1})\sqrt{1+t^2},\qquad F(t)=\beta (t)a(t)+(1-\beta (t))t.  \] It is smooth positive, satisfies $F(t)\geq |t|/\varepsilon $ for $t\leq 0$ and $F(t)\geq t$ for $t\geq 0$, and equals $t$ for $t\geq 1$. The exact smooth functional calculus of lemma 10.49.2 makes $A=\eta F[A_0/\eta ]$ a smooth positive endomorphism. Give the base the metric $\omega $ obtained by inserting $A$ into $\omega _0$. At a point its new Levi eigenvalues are \[  \frac{\gamma _ j^0}{\eta F(\gamma _ j^0/\eta )}.  \] Each lies in $[-\varepsilon ,1]$ and each labelled $j\geq q$ equals one. Hence the increasingly ordered last $n-q+1$ eigenvalues are one, irrespective of any ordering of the other fractions. When $\psi $ is exhaustive, the conformal metric in the statement satisfies $|d\psi |_{\widehat\omega }^2\leq 1$. It is complete: a Cauchy sequence has bounded $\psi $ by this Lipschitz estimate, lies in a compact sublevel, and has a convergent subsequence; smooth positive local metric comparison identifies its topology with the manifold topology, so Cauchyness gives convergence. This works on each component. Conformal change multiplies every eigenvalue by $f^{-1}$, and any $k$ indices include at least $k-q+1$ of the ones, proving ( 9.50.2 ). $\square$

title: Lemma 9.50.3
section: 9.50 Bundle cohomology on strongly convex exhaustions
text: Lemma 9.50.3 . E85E2E5CB1FF Let $(M,\omega )$ be complete Hermitian and $(G,h)$ a smooth Hermitian holomorphic bundle. In a fixed bidegree $(p,k)$ with $0\leq p\leq n$ and $1\leq k\leq n$, suppose \[  A=[\mathrm i\Theta (G,h),\Lambda _\omega ]+T_\omega \geq I,  \] where $T_\omega $ is the exterior-factor zero-order remainder in theorem 11.48.15 . Every distributionally closed $g\in L^2_{p,k}(M,G)$ has a solution $D''u=g$ with $\| u\| ^2\leq \| g\| ^2$. Its unique minimum-norm solution satisfies $\delta ''u=0$ and is smooth when $g$ is smooth. Moreover a smooth form satisfying $D''u=\delta ''u=0$ on a fixed open set obeys, for compact $K\Subset W$ in that set, 09CCAA35AAF1 9.50.4 \begin{equation}  \| u\| _{C^ r(K)}\leq C_{r,K,W}\| u\| _{L^2(W)} \qquad (r\geq 0), \end{equation} using finitely many fixed local frames. No Kähler assumption is needed. Proof. The exact complete-Hermitian domain lemma 6.26.4 supplies the closed maximal $D''$ operators, their maximal formal-adjoint domains and joint compactly supported smooth graph density in every degree/rank. Its assumptions apply to this smooth $h$, including when it contains an arbitrary smooth scalar weight: the cutoff errors are wedge and contraction by $\bar\partial \chi _ R$, whose norms depend only on the complete base metric, not derivatives of that weight. The local smooth-matrix commutator uses only bounds on each compact chart. Thus no global bound on weight derivatives is an extra premise. For compactly supported smooth $v$, the complete Hermitian energy identity theorem 11.48.15 gives \[  \| v\| ^2\leq \int \langle Av,v\rangle \leq \| D''v\| ^2+\| \delta ''v\| ^2.  \] Pass the first and last terms to the joint graph limit. With $T=D''$ from $(p,k-1)$ and $S=D''$ from $(p,k)$, this proves \[  |\langle g,v\rangle |^2\leq \| g\| ^2 (\| T^*v\| ^2+\| Sv\| ^2)  \] on the full joint domains. For $k=n$, $S=0$ into the zero space. The equality $(D'')^2=0$ gives $ST=0$ on the maximal domains. The checked closed Hilbert-complex theorem Hilbert-complex solvability from the dual energy estimate gives the solution and bound. The affine solution space has the closed direction $\ker T$, so has a unique minimum orthogonal to that kernel. The preceding $D''$ range lies in this kernel; testing its adjoint shows $\delta ''u=0$. In antiholomorphic degree zero this is automatic. We verify regularity and the quantitative local assertion. At a real covector $\xi $, the principal symbols of $D''$ and $\delta ''$ are exterior multiplication by $\xi ^{0,1}$ and its contraction. Their anticommutator is $|\xi |_\omega ^2I/2$, so the principal symbol of $\Delta ''$ is real scalar and positive, for any smooth Hermitian base and bundle metric. In coordinates its divergence principal form is $\tfrac 12\int g^{ij}H_{AB}\partial _ jv_ A \overline{\partial _ iv_ B}\, dV$. Integration by parts and absorption of the lower-order terms give, on compactly supported smooth vectors, \[  \| v\| _{H^1}^2\leq C(\| D''v\| ^2+\| \delta ''v\| ^2+\| v\| ^2).  \] Localize a weak solution by a chart cutoff. Smooth-matrix commutator approximation and this bound give a bounded $H^1$ approximation; weak derivative convergence puts it in $H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$. The equation $\Delta ''u=\delta ''g$ has smooth right-hand side. The complete finite-vector divergence regularity theorem interior regularity for elliptic systems in divergence form , followed by Sobolev spaces, duality and local embedding , yields smoothness. For the last assertion, on a slightly larger compact neighborhood the cutoff product rules and $D''u=\delta ''u=0$ bound the initial $H^1$ norm by $C\| u\| _{L^2(W)}$. The quantitative interior estimates for that same divergence system then bound every higher Sobolev norm on successively smaller neighborhoods by the same $L^2$ norm; its right-hand side is zero. The proved local Sobolev embedding gives ( 9.50.4 ). All metrics and coefficients in this last bound are fixed. $\square$

title: Theorem 9.50.5
section: 9.50 Bundle cohomology on strongly convex exhaustions
text: Theorem 9.50.5 . 8AB8E8F1EBBE Let $M$ be strongly $q$-complete and $E$ a holomorphic vector bundle, where $q\geq 1$. Then \[  H^ k(M,\mathcal O(E))=0\qquad (k\geq q).  \] Explicitly, every smooth closed $E$-valued $(0,k)$-form in this range has a smooth primitive. The statement allows non-Kähler manifolds and does not impose curvature positivity on $E$. Proof. The empty manifold, zero bundle, dimension zero and $q>n$ give no nonzero Dolbeault terms in the specified range. Otherwise take a smooth strongly $q$-convex exhaustion $\psi \geq 0$ and use lemma 9.50.1 with $\varepsilon =1/q$. Fix the resulting complete metric $\widehat\omega =f\omega $ once and for all. The pointwise line-curvature coefficient formula in proposition 10.33.6 and ( 9.50.2 ) give, on $(n,k)$ for $k\geq q$, 894DFD0DF9E2 9.50.6 \begin{equation}  [\mathcal H(\psi ),\Lambda _{\widehat\omega }] \geq (qf)^{-1}I. \end{equation} Give $E$ a fixed smooth metric, $K_ M$ its induced metric, and put $G=E\otimes K_ M^{-1}$. The fixed smooth Hermitian operators \[  A_0^{(k)}=[\mathrm i\Theta (G),\Lambda _{\widehat\omega }] +T_{\widehat\omega }\otimes I_ G \quad (q\leq k\leq n)  \] have a continuous common norm bound $C(x)\geq 0$, the maximum of their finitely many pointwise norms. This bound is finite on every compact sublevel. All derivatives of the complete conformal metric that occur in $T_{\widehat\omega }$ are already fixed; no uniform bound at infinity or limiting conformal parameter is assumed. Multiplying the bundle norm by a scalar weight cancels in every endomorphism operator norm, so this same $C(x)$ is independent of it. For a convex increasing smooth $\chi $ multiply the metric of $G$ by $e^{-\chi (\psi )}$. Tensor curvature and the chain rule give \[  \mathrm i\Theta (G_\chi )=\mathrm i\Theta (G) +\chi '(\psi )\mathcal H(\psi )I_ G +\chi ''(\psi )\mathrm i\partial \psi \wedge \bar\partial \psi I_ G.  \] The last term is a semipositive scalar curvature, whose operator on $(n,k)$ is nonnegative. Thus its torsion-curvature operator satisfies 1D0C411FD4AC 9.50.7 \begin{equation}  A_\chi ^{(k)}\geq \bigl (\chi '(\psi )/(qf)-C(x)\bigr )I. \end{equation} The torsion term has not changed: it acts on the exterior factor and depends only on the fixed base metric, by theorem 11.48.15 . We give a single weight which makes this at least $I$ in all these degrees and makes any specified smooth datum $g$ square integrable. For that datum, after the canonical-form identification below, put \[  a_ j=\int _{\{ j\leq \psi \leq j+1\} }|g|^2\, dV_{\widehat\omega }<\infty .  \] Choose nondecreasing $M_ j\geq 1$ larger than $q\sup _{\{ \psi \leq j+2\} } f(C+1)$ and than $\log (2^{j+2}(1+a_{j+1}))$. A supremum over the empty set imposes no condition. Let $\zeta $ be smooth nondecreasing, zero up to0 and one from1, and set on the real line \[  b(t)=M_0+\sum _{j\geq 0}(M_{j+1}-M_ j)\zeta (t-j),\qquad \chi (t)=\int _0^ t b(s)\, ds.  \] These sums are locally finite. On $[j,j+1]$ one has $\chi '\geq M_ j$, so ( 9.50.7 ) is at least $I$. For $j\geq 1$, $\chi (j)\geq M_{j-1}\geq \log (2^{j+1}(1+a_ j))$, giving \[  \int _ M |g|^2e^{-\chi (\psi )}\, dV_{\widehat\omega } \leq a_0+\sum _{j\geq 1}2^{-j-1}<\infty .  \] The integer bands may overlap on level sets, which only enlarges this upper bound. The construction works for compactly supported data with a weight chosen only from the geometry as well. The canonical identification from $E$-valued $(0,j)$-forms to $G$-valued $(n,j)$-forms is \[  I_ j(a\otimes v)=(a\wedge \tau )\otimes (v\otimes \tau ^{-1}),  \] where $\tau $ is a local nonzero holomorphic top form. Transition factors cancel, and appending it on the right makes $I$ commute with $D''$ without a degree sign. The induced canonical/dual metrics make it isometric. Apply lemma 9.50.3 to $I_ kg$ and the chosen weight; pull its smooth primitive back by $I_{k-1}$. This proves smooth analytic vanishing. The exact E-valued Dolbeault resolution comparison corollary 10.43.11 gives the sheaf statement. $\square$

title: 9.51 Coherent sections and Stein vanishing
section: 9.51 Coherent sections and Stein vanishing
text:
An analytic space here may be nonreduced. Its underlying space is Hausdorff with a countable basis; locally its structure sheaf is $\mathcal O_\Omega /\mathcal J$ on the zero set of a coherent ideal $\mathcal J$, with $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ N$ open. Coherent sheaves are modules over this structure sheaf. We retain the whole module and its nilpotent action in all the constructions. For scalar complex Hessians we use $\mathcal H(f)=\mathrm i\partial  ar\partial f$. Lemma 9.51.1 . 95172CE64D2D Every open $V\subset \mathbb R^ m$ admits, subordinate to any open cover, a countable locally finite open refinement of multiplicity at most $5^ m$. Consequently, for every sheaf of abelian groups $\mathcal A$ on $V$, \[  H^ k(V,\mathcal A)=0\qquad (k\geq 5^ m).  \] Only finiteness of this bound will be needed. Proof. For each $x\in V$, let $a(x)\leq 1$ be the supremum of radii $t\leq 1$ for which $\overline B(x,10t)$ is contained in one member of the prescribed cover. This is positive and lower semicontinuous: any smaller radius has a compact closure inside a slightly larger allowed ball and continues to work at nearby centers. Put \[  r(x)= rac1{100}\inf _{y\in V}\{ a(y)+|x-y|\} .  \] It is positive, at most $a(x)/100$, and $1/100$-Lipschitz. Positivity follows by bounding $a$ below on a neighborhood of $x$ and using the distance to its complement for the other $y$'s. The Lipschitz estimate follows by the triangle inequality inside the infimum. Choose a maximal disjoint family $B(x_ j,r_ j)$, $r_ j=r(x_ j)$. It is countable since disjoint open balls have distinct rational points. Every ball $B(x,r(x))$ intersects a chosen one. At an intersection the Lipschitz inequality gives $r(x)/r_ j\leq 101/99$, hence $|x-x_ j|<3r_ j$. Thus $B(x_ j,3r_ j)$ cover $V$ and are subordinate to the original cover. If $z$ lies in one of them, then \[  r(z)/1.03\leq r_ j\leq r(z)/0.97.  \] The corresponding disjoint balls all lie in $B(z,4r(z)/0.97)$. Comparing Euclidean volumes bounds their number by $(4\cdot 1.03/0.97)^ m<5^ m$. The same Lipschitz calculation for balls meeting a sufficiently small fixed neighborhood of $z$ bounds their radii above and below by positive multiples of $r(z)$ and their centers in a fixed ball. Disjoint-ball packing therefore proves local finiteness. For $m=0$ the assertion is immediate. The refinements themselves prove paracompactness. Apply the checked cover-order cohomology corollary 10.44.15 with $n=5^ m-1$. That theorem includes the alternating/full Čech homotopy and the paracompact Čech-to-Godement comparison, so repeated tuple indices cause no dimension assumption here. $\square$ Lemma 9.51.2 . 7D7D2E32D0F3 If a countable-basis complex manifold $M$ has a smooth strictly PSH exhaustion, then $H^ k(M,\mathcal O(E))=0$ for every holomorphic vector bundle $E$ and $k\geq 1$. For a smooth strictly PSH exhaustion $ho $ on $M$, restriction $\mathcal O(M)	o \mathcal O(M_ b)$, $M_ b=\{ ho <b\} $, has dense image for compact convergence, also for finite vectors of holomorphic functions. Proof. Shift the exhaustion to be nonnegative. By lemma 6.26.8 , $\omega =\mathcal H(\mathrm e^ho )$ is complete Kähler. Identify $E$-valued $(0,k)$-forms with $(n,k)$-forms valued in $ igwedge ^ n TM\otimes E$, by the evaluation pairing with a local holomorphic top form. This is a global holomorphic identification and commutes with $ ar\partial $. Give this new bundle an arbitrary smooth Hermitian metric. On every compact exhaustion band, its curvature has a finite Nakano lower bound relative to $\mathcal H(ho )$. The fast-weight construction ( 6.26.9 ) supplies a smooth convex increasing $\chi $ so that twisting by $\mathrm e^{-\chi (ho )}$ makes its curvature at least $\omega \otimes \operatorname {Id}$ in Nakano form, and makes a prescribed smooth closed datum globally weighted $L^2$. In degree $(n,k)$ the curvature operator is at least $k$, by proposition 10.33.6 . Thus its inverse energy is finite. The complete Kähler estimate theorem 6.26.5 gives a smooth primitive. For $k>n$ there are no Dolbeault forms. The full bundle Dolbeault/sheaf comparison corollary 10.43.11 proves the assertion. For density, fix $K\Subset M_ b$ and $f\in \mathcal O(M_ b)$. Choose $a<b_1<b_2<b$ with $K\subset M_ a$, and a smooth $\eta $ of compact support in $M_{b_2}$ equal to one on $M_{b_1}$. Then $g= ar\partial (\eta f)$ has compact support in $M_{b_2}\setminus M_{b_1}$ and is closed. Choose a base weight $\chi _0\circ ho $ as above for the trivial-function equation, and a smooth convex nondecreasing $	heta $ which is zero on $(-\infty ,a]$ and at least one on $[b_1,\infty )$. The weights $\chi _0\circ ho +
u 	heta \circ ho $ have the same positive curvature lower bound. Their smooth solutions $ ar\partial u_
u =g$ satisfy \[  \int _{M_ a}|u_
u |^2\mathrm e^{-\chi _0(ho )}\, dV_\omega \leq C\mathrm e^{-
u }.  \] On $M_ a$ these are holomorphic functions. The checked local submean and Cauchy estimates therefore give convergence to zero uniformly with every derivative on $K$. The global holomorphic functions $\eta f-u_
u $ approximate $f$ there. Choose an increasing compact exhaustion of $M_ b$ and make the successive errors arbitrarily small to obtain compact convergence on all of $M_ b$. Apply the construction to the finitely many coefficients for the vector assertion. $\square$ Lemma 9.51.3 . B785192891F0 Let $\mathcal F$ be coherent on an embedded analytic patch $A\subset \Omega \subset \mathbb C^ N$. For every $x\in A$ and finite $L$ there is an ambient neighborhood $W$ of $x$ and an exact sequence \[  \mathcal O_ W^{r_ L}\longrightarrow \cdots \longrightarrow \mathcal O_ W^{r_1}\longrightarrow \mathcal O_ W^{r_0} \longrightarrow i_*\mathcal F\longrightarrow 0.  \] Exactness at the first displayed term is not asserted; its kernel is coherent. If $L\geq 5^{2N}$ and $V\subset W$ has a smooth strict-PSH exhaustion, then \[  H^ k(A\cap V,\mathcal F)=0\quad (k\geq 1),\qquad \mathcal O(V)^{r_0}\longrightarrow \mathcal F(A\cap V) 	ext{is surjective}.  \] Proof. The sheaf $i_*\mathcal F$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_\Omega $-module. To check this in the nonreduced case, write $\mathcal O_ A=\mathcal O_\Omega /\mathcal J$. Finite local generators over $\mathcal O_ A$ are still generators over $\mathcal O_\Omega $. Lift finitely many generators of their relation module over $\mathcal O_ A$; together with each generator of $\mathcal J$ in each coordinate, they generate all relations over $\mathcal O_\Omega $. Thus the definition of coherence is preserved. The canonical coherent-kernel theorem kernels and exact sequences of coherent modules now applies. Choose finite local generators at $x$, shrink so they generate as a sheaf, take the coherent kernel, and repeat $L$ times. Only finitely many shrinkings occur, so the resulting neighborhood works for the entire displayed sequence. This uses local coherence, not a global-generation theorem. Write $Z_0=\ker (\mathcal O_ W^{r_0}	o i_*\mathcal F)$ and $Z_ j=\ker (\mathcal O_ W^{r_ j}	o Z_{j-1})$. The successive short exact sequences and the preceding bundle-vanishing lemma give, for $k\geq 1$, \[  H^ k(V,i_*\mathcal F)\simeq H^{k+1}(V,Z_0) \simeq \cdots \simeq H^{k+L+1}(V,Z_ L)=0.  \] The last equality follows from the finite Euclidean bound, which applies even to an arbitrary sheaf $Z_ L$. The same dimension shifting starting with $H^1(V,Z_0)$ proves that this group is zero, giving section surjectivity. For a closed embedding $i:A\cap V	o V$, direct image is exact: its stalks are the original stalks on $A$ and zero outside the closed set. It takes flabby sheaves to flabby sheaves, and global sections are unchanged. Push a flabby resolution forward and use the checked acyclic-resolution comparison to identify $H^ k(V,i_*\mathcal F)=H^ k(A\cap V,\mathcal F)$. The module calculations above use $\mathcal J$ itself and do not replace it by its radical. $\square$ Call such a sufficiently long local presentation a distinguished presentation. Small polydiscs with closure inside its ambient domain are distinguished section patches. At a point a smaller distinguished presentation of any prescribed finite length is always available. Corollary 9.51.4 . 74FAA5CBDAB7 Let $q\geq 1$, and let a distinguished patch $A\subset \Omega $ carry the sufficiently long free resolution above. If $U\subset A$ is strongly $q$-complete, or merely strongly $q$-convex, then $H^ k(U,\mathcal F)=0$ for $k\geq q$. Proof. In the second case add $C|z|^2$ to the exhaustion to remove its compact exceptional set. A finite ambient extension cover of that compact set bounds all negative Hessians there, so one $C$ makes the sum strictly PSH there. Outside it, the added positive form preserves strong $q$-convexity. Nonnegativity of the added term preserves properness. Thus $U$ is strongly $q$-complete in either case. The embedded neighborhood corollary 9.49.10 supplies a strongly $q$-complete ambient $V$ meeting $A$ precisely in $U$. The full bundle theorem 9.50.5 gives $H^ j(V,\mathcal O^{r_ i})=0$ for $j\geq q$. The same actual short exact sequences as in the local resolution lemma therefore give \[  H^ k(U,\mathcal F)\simeq H^{k+L+1}(V,Z_ L)=0 \qquad (k\geq q).  \] The last equality is the already proved finite Euclidean sheaf bound. There is no global-generation or Cartan vanishing premise in this dimension shift. $\square$ Theorem 9.51.5 . 569E973DEFD9 Every coherent sheaf on a countable-basis analytic space has intrinsic Hausdorff Fréchet section topologies. Restrictions and maps induced by coherent sheaf morphisms are continuous; the topology on sections over a union is the closed gluing subspace topology for a countable cover. On an ambient strict-PSH domain with a distinguished presentation it is exactly the quotient topology of its free section presentation. Proof. First use a distinguished polydisc $D\subset \Omega $. The preceding lemma makes $\mathcal O(D)^{r_0}	o \mathcal F(A\cap D)$ surjective. Its kernel is closed. Indeed if holomorphic tuples $f_ j$ in the kernel converge on compact sets to $f$, then at each $x\in D$ their images modulo every power of the maximal ideal converge to the corresponding image of $f_ x$, by Taylor/Cauchy coefficient convergence. The image of the relation submodule in each finite-dimensional jet quotient is closed. The canonical module Krull closure theorem Krull closure for analytic modules therefore implies that $f_ x$ is in the relation submodule. This holds at every point, so $f$ is in the kernel. Give $\mathcal F(A\cap D)$ the resulting Hausdorff Fréchet quotient topology, using proposition 2.12.1 . For each $x$, give the finite local module $\mathcal F_ x$ its Krull topology, defined by its finite-dimensional quotients $\mathcal F_ x/\mathfrak m_ x^ k\mathcal F_ x$. These are Hausdorff together: the checked module Krull intersection theorem gives $ igcap _ k\mathfrak m_ x^ k\mathcal F_ x=0$. The maximal ideal of the analytic local ring is the image of the ambient maximal ideal, so these powers and topologies are intrinsic, including for nonreduced spaces. A module morphism preserves these powers and induces linear maps of their finite-dimensional quotients, so it is continuous. Taylor coefficient continuity on the free section space shows that every germ map $\mathcal F(A\cap D)	o \mathcal F_ x$ is continuous for the quotient section topology just defined. Now restrictions, coherent morphisms and changes of presentations between such section spaces have closed graphs. Indeed, if $s_ j	o s$ in the source section space and $\phi (s_ j)|_ U	o t$ in the target, their germs satisfy $t_ x=\phi _ x(s_ x)$ for every $x\in U$, by the continuous germ maps and their Hausdorff targets. Equality of all germs is equality of sections. Thus $t=\phi (s)|_ U$. Both section spaces are Fréchet, so the closed graph theorem in proposition 2.12.1 proves continuity. Applied to the identity for two presentations or embeddings it proves equality of their topologies. This argument uses the full module germ, not merely the value on the reduced underlying set. Choose a countable basis of sufficiently small distinguished patches, refining their pairwise overlaps by patches of the same kind. Define the topology on $\mathcal F(U)$ by all restrictions to basis patches contained in $U$. A compatible family of such sections glues uniquely. The compatibility equations are closed because the restriction maps just proved continuous have Hausdorff targets. Hence this space is a closed subspace of a countable product of Fréchet spaces, and is Fréchet. The local construction implies that the topology so obtained on a basis patch is no stronger than its quotient topology. The identity is a continuous linear bijection of Fréchet spaces, and is therefore a homeomorphism by open mapping. Common basis refinements and the same closed-graph argument show independence of all chosen presentations and embeddings. They also show continuity of restrictions and coherent morphisms on arbitrary opens, and the asserted topological gluing property. Finally, on any $V$ in the preceding local vanishing lemma, the continuous free section surjection into the now intrinsic Fréchet space $\mathcal F(A\cap V)$ is open. Its quotient topology is therefore exactly this intrinsic topology. $\square$ Corollary 9.51.6 . AF9753BBA4F0 All these coherent section spaces are nuclear Fréchet. For a coherent subsheaf $\mathcal F'\subset \mathcal F$, $\mathcal F'(U)$ is a closed subspace of $\mathcal F(U)$ with its induced topology. A local section space is a closed quotient of a finite sum of nuclear holomorphic polydisc spaces. General sections are a closed gluing subspace of their countable product. Apply theorem 2.13.3 . The canonical module Krull theorem makes each $\mathcal F'_ x$ closed in $\mathcal F_ x$: the intersection of $\mathcal F'_ x+\mathfrak m_ x^ k\mathcal F_ x$ is $\mathcal F'_ x$, and each of these sets is closed in the Krull topology through a finite-dimensional quotient. Thus $\mathcal F'(U)$ is the intersection of the inverse images of these closed submodules under the continuous germ maps. Inclusion is continuous; open mapping onto this closed Fréchet image identifies its topology with the induced one. For concentric distinguished polydiscs $D'\Subset D$, restriction of free sections is nuclear, by the explicit larger-to-smaller polydisc nuclear series in theorem 2.13.4 and its Banach factorization. It is therefore compact. Let $q,q'$ be the free section quotient maps. Choose a zero neighborhood $B$ in the first free section space with compact restriction image closure. Then $q(B)$ is a zero neighborhood by open mapping, and the restriction of $q(B)$ has compact closure in the target quotient, as the continuous image under $q'$ of that compact free-section closure. Thus local coherent restriction is compact as well. For general $U'\Subset U$, cover $\overline{U'}$ by finitely many smaller distinguished patches $W'_ a\Subset W_ a\subset U$ of this kind. The map to $\prod _ a\mathcal F(W'_ a)$ obtained by restriction from $U$ is compact: factor it through $\prod _ a\mathcal F(W_ a)$ and use finitely many compact restriction neighborhoods. The closure of its image lies in the closed compatibility subspace identified with $\mathcal F( igcup _ aW'_ a)$. The inverse gluing map and restriction to $U'$ are continuous. Their composition proves the assertion. $\square$

title: Lemma 9.51.1
section: 9.51 Coherent sections and Stein vanishing
text: Lemma 9.51.1 . 95172CE64D2D Every open $V\subset \mathbb R^ m$ admits, subordinate to any open cover, a countable locally finite open refinement of multiplicity at most $5^ m$. Consequently, for every sheaf of abelian groups $\mathcal A$ on $V$, \[  H^ k(V,\mathcal A)=0\qquad (k\geq 5^ m).  \] Only finiteness of this bound will be needed. Proof. For each $x\in V$, let $a(x)\leq 1$ be the supremum of radii $t\leq 1$ for which $\overline B(x,10t)$ is contained in one member of the prescribed cover. This is positive and lower semicontinuous: any smaller radius has a compact closure inside a slightly larger allowed ball and continues to work at nearby centers. Put \[  r(x)=\frac1{100}\inf _{y\in V}\{ a(y)+|x-y|\} .  \] It is positive, at most $a(x)/100$, and $1/100$-Lipschitz. Positivity follows by bounding $a$ below on a neighborhood of $x$ and using the distance to its complement for the other $y$'s. The Lipschitz estimate follows by the triangle inequality inside the infimum. Choose a maximal disjoint family $B(x_ j,r_ j)$, $r_ j=r(x_ j)$. It is countable since disjoint open balls have distinct rational points. Every ball $B(x,r(x))$ intersects a chosen one. At an intersection the Lipschitz inequality gives $r(x)/r_ j\leq 101/99$, hence $|x-x_ j|<3r_ j$. Thus $B(x_ j,3r_ j)$ cover $V$ and are subordinate to the original cover. If $z$ lies in one of them, then \[  r(z)/1.03\leq r_ j\leq r(z)/0.97.  \] The corresponding disjoint balls all lie in $B(z,4r(z)/0.97)$. Comparing Euclidean volumes bounds their number by $(4\cdot 1.03/0.97)^ m<5^ m$. The same Lipschitz calculation for balls meeting a sufficiently small fixed neighborhood of $z$ bounds their radii above and below by positive multiples of $r(z)$ and their centers in a fixed ball. Disjoint-ball packing therefore proves local finiteness. For $m=0$ the assertion is immediate. The refinements themselves prove paracompactness. Apply the checked cover-order cohomology corollary 10.44.15 with $n=5^ m-1$. That theorem includes the alternating/full Čech homotopy and the paracompact Čech-to-Godement comparison, so repeated tuple indices cause no dimension assumption here. $\square$

title: Lemma 9.51.3
section: 9.51 Coherent sections and Stein vanishing
text: Lemma 9.51.3 . B785192891F0 Let $\mathcal F$ be coherent on an embedded analytic patch $A\subset \Omega \subset \mathbb C^ N$. For every $x\in A$ and finite $L$ there is an ambient neighborhood $W$ of $x$ and an exact sequence \[  \mathcal O_ W^{r_ L}\longrightarrow \cdots \longrightarrow \mathcal O_ W^{r_1}\longrightarrow \mathcal O_ W^{r_0} \longrightarrow i_*\mathcal F\longrightarrow 0.  \] Exactness at the first displayed term is not asserted; its kernel is coherent. If $L\geq 5^{2N}$ and $V\subset W$ has a smooth strict-PSH exhaustion, then \[  H^ k(A\cap V,\mathcal F)=0\quad (k\geq 1),\qquad \mathcal O(V)^{r_0}\longrightarrow \mathcal F(A\cap V) \text{is surjective}.  \] Proof. The sheaf $i_*\mathcal F$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_\Omega $-module. To check this in the nonreduced case, write $\mathcal O_ A=\mathcal O_\Omega /\mathcal J$. Finite local generators over $\mathcal O_ A$ are still generators over $\mathcal O_\Omega $. Lift finitely many generators of their relation module over $\mathcal O_ A$; together with each generator of $\mathcal J$ in each coordinate, they generate all relations over $\mathcal O_\Omega $. Thus the definition of coherence is preserved. The canonical coherent-kernel theorem kernels and exact sequences of coherent modules now applies. Choose finite local generators at $x$, shrink so they generate as a sheaf, take the coherent kernel, and repeat $L$ times. Only finitely many shrinkings occur, so the resulting neighborhood works for the entire displayed sequence. This uses local coherence, not a global-generation theorem. Write $Z_0=\ker (\mathcal O_ W^{r_0}\to i_*\mathcal F)$ and $Z_ j=\ker (\mathcal O_ W^{r_ j}\to Z_{j-1})$. The successive short exact sequences and the preceding bundle-vanishing lemma give, for $k\geq 1$, \[  H^ k(V,i_*\mathcal F)\simeq H^{k+1}(V,Z_0) \simeq \cdots \simeq H^{k+L+1}(V,Z_ L)=0.  \] The last equality follows from the finite Euclidean bound, which applies even to an arbitrary sheaf $Z_ L$. The same dimension shifting starting with $H^1(V,Z_0)$ proves that this group is zero, giving section surjectivity. For a closed embedding $i:A\cap V\to V$, direct image is exact: its stalks are the original stalks on $A$ and zero outside the closed set. It takes flabby sheaves to flabby sheaves, and global sections are unchanged. Push a flabby resolution forward and use the checked acyclic-resolution comparison to identify $H^ k(V,i_*\mathcal F)=H^ k(A\cap V,\mathcal F)$. The module calculations above use $\mathcal J$ itself and do not replace it by its radical. $\square$

title: Corollary 9.51.4
section: 9.51 Coherent sections and Stein vanishing
text: Corollary 9.51.4 . 74FAA5CBDAB7 Let $q\geq 1$, and let a distinguished patch $A\subset \Omega $ carry the sufficiently long free resolution above. If $U\subset A$ is strongly $q$-complete, or merely strongly $q$-convex, then $H^ k(U,\mathcal F)=0$ for $k\geq q$. Proof. In the second case add $C|z|^2$ to the exhaustion to remove its compact exceptional set. A finite ambient extension cover of that compact set bounds all negative Hessians there, so one $C$ makes the sum strictly PSH there. Outside it, the added positive form preserves strong $q$-convexity. Nonnegativity of the added term preserves properness. Thus $U$ is strongly $q$-complete in either case. The embedded neighborhood corollary 9.49.10 supplies a strongly $q$-complete ambient $V$ meeting $A$ precisely in $U$. The full bundle theorem 9.50.5 gives $H^ j(V,\mathcal O^{r_ i})=0$ for $j\geq q$. The same actual short exact sequences as in the local resolution lemma therefore give \[  H^ k(U,\mathcal F)\simeq H^{k+L+1}(V,Z_ L)=0 \qquad (k\geq q).  \] The last equality is the already proved finite Euclidean sheaf bound. There is no global-generation or Cartan vanishing premise in this dimension shift. $\square$

Applied to the identity for two presentations or embeddings it proves equality of their topologies. This argument uses the full module germ, not merely the value on the reduced underlying set. Choose a countable basis of sufficiently small distinguished patches, refining their pairwise overlaps by patches of the same kind. The compatibility equations are closed because the restriction maps just proved continuous have Hausdorff targets. title: 9.51.7 Acyclic patches and cohomology topologies
section: 9.51 Coherent sections and Stein vanishing
text:
We use the analytic ambient-neighborhood theorem 9.49.8 in its $q=1$ case, with the strict-PSH extension and embedding invariance proved with it. If $U$ is a strongly $1$-complete open subset of a distinguished patch $A\subset \Omega $, first replace $\Omega $ by an ambient open set meeting $A$ precisely in $U$. The set $U$ is then closed analytic in that ambient space. The theorem supplies a strongly $1$-complete ambient open $V$ meeting $A$ precisely in $U$. The distinguished free resolution restricts to $V$, so lemma 9.51.3 gives $H^ k(U,\mathcal F)=0$ for $k\geq 1$ and an open free section surjection. The same holds if $U$ is only strongly $1$-convex in an embedded patch: add $C|z|^2$ to its exhaustion. On the exceptional compact set finitely many ambient smooth extensions have bounded negative Hessian, which the Euclidean term dominates for one sufficiently large $C$. Outside that set it preserves strict positivity. Its nonnegativity preserves the exhaustion property. Small distinguished polydisc patches are strongly $1$-complete, with the sum of the usual reciprocal boundary-distance exhaustions. Finite intersections of strongly $1$-complete opens are strongly $1$-complete: make each exhaustion nonnegative and add them on the intersection. A bounded sublevel lies in the compact sublevel of each summand, hence is compact in the intersection. Positivity follows by local ambient extension in a common embedding. An intersection of distinguished patches lies in the first such patch, so the preceding ambient argument makes it acyclic for $\mathcal F$. We can consequently choose countable acyclic covers and a countable acyclic basis, with common acyclic refinements. Give $H^ k(U,\mathcal F)$ the quotient topology of its cycle space in the Fréchet Čech complex of any such cover. The canonical acyclic-cover comparison theorem 10.43.16 identifies this with sheaf cohomology. Refinement maps are continuous cochain maps and induce cohomology bijections. By theorem 2.12.5 , their induced maps are open, even if these quotient spaces are not Hausdorff. The topology is therefore independent of the cover. Restrictions and coherent morphisms act continuously: refine by an acyclic basis on which their cochain maps are the already continuous section restrictions or morphisms. The same topology is obtained from any countable acyclic cover: refine it by the acyclic basis, use the algebraic acyclic-cover comparison, and apply the same cohomological openness. In particular the closed-embedding identification $H^ k(V,i_*\mathcal F)=H^ k(A\cap V,\mathcal F)$ is topological. Choose an acyclic cover for $i_*\mathcal F$ on $V$. Its intersections with $A$ are acyclic by the flabby direct-image comparison above. The two Čech complexes have identical section spaces and differentials; their section topologies coincide by the intrinsic germ construction. Thus their cohomology identification preserves the specified quotient topologies. For a holomorphic vector bundle $E$ on a complex manifold, this topology agrees with the smooth Dolbeault quotient topology. Use the double complex of smooth $E$-valued $(0,j)$-forms on the intersections of an acyclic basis. Its terms, with their compact $C^\infty $ seminorms and countable products, are Fréchet. The augmented horizontal rows are exact by the checked partition-of-unity Čech contraction; that contraction is continuous because only finitely many partition supports meet each fixed compact set. The augmented vertical columns are exact by the full bundle Dolbeault comparison and the just proved bundle vanishing on the strongly $1$-complete intersections. The finite-diagonal comparison lemma therefore makes the two augmentations, from the global Dolbeault complex and from the holomorphic Čech complex, cohomology bijections. They are continuous: restrictions are continuous, and holomorphic-to-smooth inclusion is continuous by local Cauchy estimates. Cohomological openness makes both maps topological isomorphisms on quotient cohomology, including non-Hausdorff cases. Lemma 9.51.8 . 403B48857D12 In a distinguished patch $A\subset \Omega $, let $U'\subset U$ be $q$-Runge complete: each compact $L\subset U'$ lies in $\{ \psi <b\} \Subset U'$ for a smooth strongly $q$-convex exhaustion $\psi $ of $U$. Then $H^{q-1}(U,\mathcal F)	o H^{q-1}(U',\mathcal F)$ has dense image, with the quotient cohomology topologies. Proof. Apply corollary 9.49.10 , including its Runge clause, to $U$ after restricting the ambient open set to meet $A$ exactly in $U$. For each compact $L\subset U'$ it supplies a strongly $q$-complete ambient $V$, with $A\cap V=U$, and an exhaustion sublevel $V_ b$ such that $L\subset U_ b=A\cap V_ b\Subset U'$. Free presentation and dimension shifting give $H^ q(V,Z_0)=H^ q(V_ b,Z_0)=0$. Thus the free-to-coherent maps in degree $q-1$ are surjective and continuous. The bundle approximation theorem and topological Dolbeault comparison make restriction $H^{q-1}(V,\mathcal O^{r_0})	o H^{q-1}(V_ b,\mathcal O^{r_0})$ dense. Its commuting square with the two presentation maps proves density from $U$ to $U_ b$. Choose such sets $U_{b_
u }$ increasingly, with compact closures nested in the next one and exhausting $U'$: at each step include the previous compact closure and the next compact of a fixed exhaustion in $L$. Use one countable acyclic basis $\mathcal W$ of relatively compact patches on $U$. Its subfamilies with closures in $U_{b_
u }$ give Fréchet Čech complexes $E_
u $ with surjective coordinate projections. Their inverse limit is the complex on the subfamily with closures in $U'$. The map from $F=\check C^ ullet (\mathcal W,\mathcal F)$ to this limit is degreewise surjective: it forgets components, and every remaining cochain extends by zero on omitted tuples. The just proved cohomology density holds at every stage. Apply theorem 2.14.6 (4). This proves density on $U'$ itself, without assuming closed boundary spaces or commuting completion with cohomology. $\square$ Lemma 9.51.9 . 600DE1CB7CE6 For arbitrary open $G,U$ in an analytic space, their ordinary sheaf Mayer–Vietoris sequence has continuous maps for these cohomology topologies. Whenever its cohomology difference map is surjective, that map is open, including on non-Hausdorff quotient cohomology. Proof. Take a countable distinguished acyclic basis $\mathcal W$ on $G\cup U$, retaining members contained in $G$ or $U$. Let $\mathcal W_ G,\mathcal W_ U$ be the subfamilies contained in $G,U$, and $\mathcal W_0=\mathcal W_ G\cap \mathcal W_ U$. They are acyclic covers of $G,U,G\cap U$. Put $A=\check C^ ullet (\mathcal W_ G,\mathcal F)\oplus \check C^ ullet (\mathcal W_ U,\mathcal F)$, $B=\check C^ ullet (\mathcal W_0,\mathcal F)$, and let $r:A	o B$ be restriction difference. Form the complex \[  K^ n=A^ n\oplus B^{n-1},\qquad D(a,b)=(da,ra-db),\qquad B^{-1}=0.  \] The map $\check C^ ullet (\mathcal W,\mathcal F)	o K$ given by the two restrictions and zero in $B^{n-1}$ is continuous and induces the ordinary Mayer–Vietoris identification $H^*(K)=H^*(G\cup U,\mathcal F)$. Here is an explicit verification of this identification. Resolve $\mathcal F$ by its checked Godement resolution $\mathcal I^ ullet $. On each of the three acyclic covers, the augmented resolution columns are exact, as in the acyclic-cover comparison. Thus the double total with entries $K^ n(\mathcal I^ j)$ computes $H^*(K(\mathcal F))$. For fixed $j$, flabby Cech acyclicity computes the row's cohomology as that of \[  \mathcal I^ j(G)\oplus \mathcal I^ j(U) \longrightarrow \mathcal I^ j(G\cap U).  \] The last map is onto by flabbiness and its kernel is $\mathcal I^ j(G\cup U)$ by gluing. Hence these rows are exact after that augmentation. The actual finite-diagonal comparison lemma identifies the same total with $\mathcal I^ ullet (G\cup U)$. The continuous map above, used also on Godement terms, agrees with the identity on that augmented resolution. It therefore induces this canonical cohomology bijection. Both source and target are Fréchet complexes, so cohomological openness makes it a topological identification. The degreewise strict sequence $0	o B[-1]	o K	o A	o 0$ gives the continuous cohomology connecting maps: pull back the last complex's closed cycle space, use the open surjection from that Fréchet preimage, and descend the lifted differential. This is the continuous long-exact construction already proved in section 9.41 . The lift formula and its Godement comparison give the usual sheaf Mayer–Vietoris maps, up to the common choice of difference sign. The difference map is induced by the continuous cochain map $r:A	o B$; if it is onto on cohomology, theorem 2.12.5 makes it open. $\square$ Theorem 9.51.10 (Compact coherent finiteness) . 7C6C814BF9A5 For a coherent sheaf $\mathcal F$ on a compact analytic space, every $H^ k(X,\mathcal F)$ is Hausdorff and finite dimensional. Proof. Choose finitely many distinguished polydisc patches $U_ a$ and smaller concentric patches $U'_ a\Subset U_ a$ still covering $X$. Both covers and their finite intersections are acyclic, as proved above. For every tuple $I$, $U'_ I\Subset U_ I$: its closure is contained in the compact intersection of the individual smaller closures inside $U_ I$. The restriction $\mathcal F(U_ I)	o \mathcal F(U'_ I)$ is compact by corollary 9.51.6 . In each fixed degree there are only finitely many tuples, so the Čech cochain restriction is a compact map on one zero neighborhood. It induces a cohomology bijection by the acyclic-cover comparison. The full Fréchet-complex compact cohomology criterion theorem 2.12.5 gives the claim in each degree. Nilpotents were retained throughout the section constructions and the sheaf exactness arguments. $\square$ Lemma 9.51.11 . 7305161C3E98 Let $q\geq 1$, let $X$ have a smooth exhaustion $\psi $ strongly $q$-convex outside a compact set $K$, and choose $c<d$ with $K\subset X_ c$. There is a finite chain \[  X_ c=G_0\subset G_1\subset \cdots \subset G_ s=X_ d  \] of sublevel sets of smooth exhaustions strongly $q$-convex outside $K$, where $G_{j+1}=G_ j\cup U_ j$. The sets $U_ j$ and $G_ j\cap U_ j$ lie in one distinguished patch, are strongly $q$-complete, and the intersection is $q$-Runge complete in $U_ j$. They have zero cohomology in degrees $k\geq q$, and restriction \[  H^{q-1}(U_ j,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^{q-1}(G_ j\cap U_ j,\mathcal F)  \] has dense image for their quotient cohomology topologies. title: Lemma 9.51.9
section: 9.51 Coherent sections and Stein vanishing
text: Lemma 9.51.9 . 600DE1CB7CE6 For arbitrary open $G,U$ in an analytic space, their ordinary sheaf Mayer–Vietoris sequence has continuous maps for these cohomology topologies. Whenever its cohomology difference map is surjective, that map is open, including on non-Hausdorff quotient cohomology. Proof. Take a countable distinguished acyclic basis $\mathcal W$ on $G\cup U$, retaining members contained in $G$ or $U$. Let $\mathcal W_ G,\mathcal W_ U$ be the subfamilies contained in $G,U$, and $\mathcal W_0=\mathcal W_ G\cap \mathcal W_ U$. They are acyclic covers of $G,U,G\cap U$. Put $A=\check C^\bullet (\mathcal W_ G,\mathcal F)\oplus \check C^\bullet (\mathcal W_ U,\mathcal F)$, $B=\check C^\bullet (\mathcal W_0,\mathcal F)$, and let $r:A\to B$ be restriction difference. Form the complex \[  K^ n=A^ n\oplus B^{n-1},\qquad D(a,b)=(da,ra-db),\qquad B^{-1}=0.  \] The map $\check C^\bullet (\mathcal W,\mathcal F)\to K$ given by the two restrictions and zero in $B^{n-1}$ is continuous and induces the ordinary Mayer–Vietoris identification $H^*(K)=H^*(G\cup U,\mathcal F)$. Here is an explicit verification of this identification. Resolve $\mathcal F$ by its checked Godement resolution $\mathcal I^\bullet $. On each of the three acyclic covers, the augmented resolution columns are exact, as in the acyclic-cover comparison. Thus the double total with entries $K^ n(\mathcal I^ j)$ computes $H^*(K(\mathcal F))$. For fixed $j$, flabby Cech acyclicity computes the row's cohomology as that of \[  \mathcal I^ j(G)\oplus \mathcal I^ j(U) \longrightarrow \mathcal I^ j(G\cap U).  \] The last map is onto by flabbiness and its kernel is $\mathcal I^ j(G\cup U)$ by gluing. Hence these rows are exact after that augmentation. The actual finite-diagonal comparison lemma identifies the same total with $\mathcal I^\bullet (G\cup U)$. The continuous map above, used also on Godement terms, agrees with the identity on that augmented resolution. It therefore induces this canonical cohomology bijection. Both source and target are Fréchet complexes, so cohomological openness makes it a topological identification. The degreewise strict sequence $0\to B[-1]\to K\to A\to 0$ gives the continuous cohomology connecting maps: pull back the last complex's closed cycle space, use the open surjection from that Fréchet preimage, and descend the lifted differential. This is the continuous long-exact construction already proved in section 9.41 . The lift formula and its Godement comparison give the usual sheaf Mayer–Vietoris maps, up to the common choice of difference sign. The difference map is induced by the continuous cochain map $r:A\to B$; if it is onto on cohomology, theorem 2.12.5 makes it open. $\square$

title: Theorem 9.51.10 (Compact coherent finiteness)
section: 9.51 Coherent sections and Stein vanishing
text: Theorem 9.51.10 (Compact coherent finiteness) . 7C6C814BF9A5 For a coherent sheaf $\mathcal F$ on a compact analytic space, every $H^ k(X,\mathcal F)$ is Hausdorff and finite dimensional. Proof. Choose finitely many distinguished polydisc patches $U_ a$ and smaller concentric patches $U'_ a\Subset U_ a$ still covering $X$. Both covers and their finite intersections are acyclic, as proved above. Nilpotents were retained throughout the section constructions and the sheaf exactness arguments. $\square$
